pull_request.title: fix(git): resolve push remote names before literal URLs
pull_request.body:
`branch.<name>.pushRemote` accepts both remote names and literal destinations. The prefix heuristic treats a configured remote named `git@mirror` as a URL, but treats an SCP URL with a different SSH user as a remote name. CI lookup can consequently use the wrong repository or fall back to the primary remote.

Ask Git to resolve a named remote in the repository's discovery context before preserving an unresolved literal. Use the structured missing-remote exit status; other Git failures remain unresolved. Cache these results separately from fetch lookups so a cached missing named remote cannot erase a literal destination. This retains the existing logical forge URL behavior, including demos that redirect push transport with `pushInsteadOf`.

Validation: Rust 1.98.0 integration tests for the complete `default_branch` module: 46 passed. Coverage includes custom SSH users, `git@mirror` and slash-named remotes, file/local paths, linked-worktree-only remote configuration, cached fetch misses and successful fetch-cache reuse, malformed Git configuration, and the existing logical forge URL with local push transport. Four of the six remote/literal cases fail against the original implementation. `cargo fmt --all` and `git diff --check` pass.

The full project pre-merge hook did not pass locally: `pre-commit` and `cargo-insta` are unavailable. The macOS SDK14.4 build also emits a nonfatal `rust-objcopy` packaging warning about its bundled `libLLVM.dylib`. Hosted validation is pending. No full-platform or live forge acceptance is claimed.
